analysis: The supplied units are head-text excerpts of docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (lines 582-1210). The only changed lines in this PR are head 198-215, a new section on WebSocket close codes and the reconnect wait. Those lines are outside the supplied units, but the patch excerpt is complete and I examined it. It is documentation only: no code, wire fields, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache behavior changes. The section says the provider reads only the close code, not the reason. Code 1012 gets a randomized fixed-range wait without backoff growth. Any other close, or no close frame, uses growing exponential backoff. A session stable for stableSessionDuration or longer resets the backoff, and each reconnect sends a fresh register. This describes the TB-002 coordinator-to-provider reconnect behavior and does not weaken any threat-model control. The coordinator is trusted, so a coordinator-sent 1012 only influences provider retry timing. A network attacker able to inject a close frame could bias reconnect timing, but that is a pre-existing availability concern. The documented jitter range and the stable-session reset limit reconnect storms and do not create new attack surface. Fresh register on every reconnect preserves the attestation and challenge flow. The surrounding unchanged protocol text (service reservations, prefix_cache v2 receipts, models_replace fencing, error sanitization) was read for context. It matches the existing T-041 cache posture: nonce, sequence and scope checks, with a stale routing hint never granting a hit. I found no regression or contradiction with the threat model. Unverified contract: the actual CoordinatorReconnectPolicy.swift implementation and its constants are not supplied, so the doc's accuracy against code is unchecked; this has no security impact.
